title: Best Indoor Pool Dehumidifiers (2026) for Pool & Spa Rooms
h1: The Best Indoor Pool Dehumidifiers for Pool Rooms and Spas
dek: An open pool never stops evaporating, and the air above it is laced with chlorine. Ordinary dehumidifiers don't last long there — these are built for it.
description: The best indoor pool dehumidifiers for home pool rooms and spa enclosures: corrosion-resistant, high-capacity units sized for constant evaporation.
intro: Choosing an **indoor pool dehumidifier** isn't like buying one for a basement or bedroom, where humidity rises and falls with the weather. A pool room never gets a break. The open water evaporates around the clock — ASHRAE's modeling puts a 75-by-25-foot indoor pool at roughly **52 pounds (about 6 gallons) of water an hour**, even with the room held at a healthy 50% humidity.

Then there's the chemistry. Chlorine and other pool chemicals off-gas into that damp air and attack the bare metal coils inside a standard dehumidifier, often wearing one out within a season or two. So a pool room dehumidifier needs two things a typical unit lacks: continuous-duty capacity and a coil that's protected against corrosion. Every pick below is chosen on those two points.
topPicksLead: For most home pool rooms and spa enclosures, the **AlorAir Sentinel HDi90** is the one to buy: commercial capacity, an epoxy-coated coil and a ductable design that keeps the unit out of the splash zone.

Evaporation from a 75×25-ft pool with the room at 50% humidity
The same pool's evaporation if the room drops below 30%

blocks.text: Notice the last two numbers. Running a pool room too dry doesn't help — it makes the water evaporate faster, which raises your make-up water and chemical bills and makes swimmers shiver as they climb out. Design guidance for natatoriums also calls for four to six air changes an hour, far more than any ordinary room.

sections.heading: How we pick pool room dehumidifiers

blocks.text: We don't test equipment in a lab. We start with manufacturer ratings (AHAM and DOE capacity), coil construction and warranty terms, then check ASHRAE guidance on pool-room humidity and evaporation, the CPSC recall database and owner reports on long-term corrosion and pump failures.

For this guide we weighted corrosion protection and continuous-duty capacity above everything else, followed by ductability, drainage and warranty length. Price mattered last: a cheap unit that corrodes out in a year isn't a bargain.

sections.heading: What to look for in a pool room dehumidifier

items.label: A protected coil
items.text: Look for an epoxy-coated or corrosion-resistant coil. Bare metal coils pit and leak in chlorinated air.

items.label: Continuous-duty capacity
items.text: Size to the pool's evaporation, not just the floor area. A spa enclosure might manage on 55 pints; a lap pool needs 90 to 130 or more.

items.label: Ductability
items.text: A ducted unit can sit in a mechanical room next door, away from splashes and fumes.

items.label: Hands-off drainage
items.text: A pump or gravity drain is essential — nobody should empty a bucket in a room that produces gallons an hour.

items.label: A target of 50–60%
items.text: Don't chase lower numbers. Our [humidistat settings guide](/guides/dehumidifier-humidistat-settings-guide/) explains how to set and verify a target.

blocks.title: When to call in an HVAC pro
blocks.text: Large or heavily used indoor pools are usually handled by a dedicated pool dehumidification system designed with the room's ventilation, heating and air changes in mind. If your pool is big, or you're building new, get a load calculation from a contractor before buying any unit off the shelf.

sections.heading: Ways to cut the moisture load in a swimming pool room

items: **Cover the pool when it's not in use.** A cover dramatically reduces evaporation and is the single cheapest humidity fix.
**Keep the air a little warmer than the water.** A room that's colder than the pool encourages faster evaporation and more condensation.
**Keep air moving.** Ventilation and ceiling fans help prevent damp pockets on glass and in corners.

**Watch the windows.** Persistent condensation on glazing is an early sign the dehumidifier is undersized. See our guide to [condensation on windows](/guides/dehumidifier-for-condensation-on-windows/).

blocks.text: If your enclosure is mostly glass, our [sunroom picks](/best/best-dehumidifier-for-sunroom/) cover the heat and condensation issues that come with it.

The **AlorAir Sentinel HDi90** is the best indoor pool dehumidifier for most home pool rooms, combining continuous commercial capacity with an epoxy-coated coil and a ductable design. Step up to the **Aprilaire E130** for a large lap-pool room, size down to the **AlorAir Sentinel HD55** for a spa or hot-tub enclosure, and use a standard portable like the **Frigidaire FHDD5034Y1** only in a small, occasionally used spa room. For even bigger spaces, see our [commercial dehumidifier picks](/best/best-commercial-dehumidifier/).

faqs.q: What is the best dehumidifier for an indoor pool room?
faqs.a: For most home pool rooms, the AlorAir Sentinel HDi90. It's rated at 90 pints a day (AHAM), has an epoxy-coated coil that resists chlorine corrosion, and can be ducted so the unit sits outside the pool room. For a larger lap pool, the Aprilaire E130 adds capacity.

faqs.q: What humidity should an indoor pool room be?
faqs.a: ASHRAE recommends 50–60% relative humidity, with about 55% as the ideal. Above 60%, condensation and mold become hard to control; below 50%, swimmers feel chilled and the pool loses more water to evaporation.

faqs.q: Do I need a special dehumidifier for a swimming pool room?
faqs.a: Yes. A pool room needs a unit built for continuous duty with a corrosion-protected coil. Standard dehumidifiers are sized for intermittent moisture and their bare coils corrode quickly in chlorinated air.

faqs.q: Can I use a portable dehumidifier in a pool room?
faqs.a: Only in a small, occasionally used spa or hot-tub room with good ventilation. A standard portable lacks corrosion protection and continuous-duty capacity, so it will wear out quickly beside a full-time pool.

faqs.q: How big a dehumidifier do I need for an indoor pool?
faqs.a: It depends on the pool's surface area, water and air temperatures, and whether you use a cover. As a rough guide, a spa enclosure may need about 55 pints a day, a modest home pool about 90, and a large lap pool 130 or more.

faqs.q: Does a pool cover reduce the need for a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: It reduces it a lot. Covering the pool when it's not in use cuts evaporation sharply, which lets a dehumidifier keep up more easily and lowers heating and chemical costs.
